paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, comparing accuracy across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis represents "Co-occurrence Number" on a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 3 to beyond 10³, with tick marks at 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis represents "ACC (%)" on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 37% to 65%, with tick marks at intervals of 5 percentage points. Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different method. The "Base" line (black with circle markers, solid) starts at approximately 37% at the lowest co-occurrence number, rises to about 41.5% near co-occurrence 30, increases to roughly 43.5% around co-occurrence 300, and then plateaus at approximately 43.5% at the highest co-occurrence values. The "FT" line (light blue with downward-pointing triangle markers, solid) begins at approximately 39.5%, rises to about 42% near co-occurrence 30, increases to roughly 46% around 300, and reaches approximately 47.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. The "IKE" line (red with upward-pointing triangle markers, solid) starts at approximately 43%, increases to about 44.5% near co-occurrence 30, rises to roughly 46% around 300, and reaches approximately 49% at the highest values. The "MEND" line (brown with diamond markers, solid) begins at approximately 44.5%, rises to about 48.5% near co-occurrence 30, increases to roughly 54% around 300, and reaches approximately 56.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. The "MEMIT" line (purple with pentagon markers, solid) starts at approximately 43.5%, increases to about 51% near co-occurrence 30, rises to roughly 53% around 300, and reaches approximately 55% at the highest values. The "ROME" line (green with square markers, solid) begins at approximately 51%, rises to about 57% near co-occurrence 30, increases to roughly 62% around 300, and reaches approximately 66% at the highest co-occurrence number. All six lines exhibit a generally increasing trend across the x-axis, with ROME maintaining the highest position throughout and Base remaining the lowest.
